title: Knowledge check: Accessibility Fundamentals in Vue

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Accessibility Fundamentals in Vue”?
options: Use color alone to communicate an error.
Remove focus indication to keep the interface visually simple.
Use a placeholder instead of a permanent label in every form.
Use semantic elements, accessible names, visible keyboard focus, clear text errors, and meaningful status announcements.
questions.answer_key: Use semantic elements, accessible names, visible keyboard focus, clear text errors, and meaningful status announcements.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Accessibility Fundamentals in Vue directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Semantic HTML”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A hidden frontend button enforces authorization.
Color is enough to identify every form error.
Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
Use v-html for all user-supplied strings.
questions.answer_key: Use safe text interpolation, semantic controls, accessible names, and enforce sensitive access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Semantic HTML”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Accessibility Fundamentals in Vue” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
